proposed.text: Under PD 1096, Rule VIII, Sec. 803, what does MACA (Maximum Allowable Construction Area) represent, and how is it calculated?

options.text: MACA equals PSO alone — it is another name for the building footprint percentage, excluding open paved areas
MACA equals PSO plus ISA — the total of building footprint percentage and impervious paved open area percentage
MACA equals TOSL minus USA — subtracting the unpaved softscape from total open space to find hard coverage
MACA equals TLA minus TOSL — total lot area less total open space, expressed as a square meter figure

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: MACA = PSO + ISA: the sum of the building footprint percentage (PSO) and the impervious paved open area percentage (ISA). It represents all hard/impervious coverage on the ground — building plus paving. Option A confuses MACA with PSO. Option C is algebraically equivalent but expressed incorrectly (TOSL − USA = ISA, not MACA). Option D mixes percentage and area units and arrives at MACA incorrectly.
proposed.explanation: Four governing equations: PSO + TOSL = 100%; TOSL = ISA + USA; MACA = PSO + ISA; TLA% = MACA + USA. MACA caps all hard/impervious coverage (building + paving) combined. For Basic R-2 without firewall: PSO=55%, ISA=30%, MACA=85% — the building plus all paving cannot exceed 85% of the lot.
proposed.code_citation: PD 1096, Rule VIII, Sec. 803.3–803.4, Table VIII.1
